methodology.fixtureSoftware: software_supplement offers a labeled fixture order-summary tool (eligibility and orders only) because the compiled context.v1 contract cannot return a valid partial result. Its rows use live agent inference but are excluded from Foundry-capability aggregates and paired comparisons.
methodology.callLedger: Each agent tool call is recorded separately with its business reads, duplicate/redundant/unnecessary flags and latency. Each completed model response is recorded with tokens, API-equivalent cost and the tool calls it issued.
methodology.registryIsolation: Each request forks the same actually validated, approved and shadowed SQLite snapshot; real quarantine is applied to its own fork.
methodology.partialAndNoContext: Compiled prefetch is inapplicable; fixed compiled arms use original tools. Handwritten prefetch can load known partial reads.
methodology.latency: Includes selector, SDK network, guards, reads, model work, provider thread archive and telemetry. Excludes per-request test database/server fixture initialization and teardown, which are in total experiment time.
methodology.replyChecks: Independent structured evidence/action labels, permitted/required reads, delay/order grounding and prohibited financial-action claims; no private reasoning or LLM judge.
methodology.uncertainty: Descriptive paired case-block bootstrap, retaining repeats together. Eleven or twelve synthetic case blocks are not a production workload sample; no production p95 claim.

Delayed delivery support generally starts by checking the order’s current delivery status and how late it is. Support teams may prioritize the most delayed order and review whether the situation fits the applicable delivery-delay policy. Depending on the circumstances, the next step may be delivery assistance, operator review, or refund-review consideration. This explanation is general only; no customer records are needed, and it does not approve, guarantee, or issue any refund or order change.

Delayed delivery support starts by checking verified account records when a customer asks about a specific order. Support looks for the order with the greatest delay, using the lowest order ID if delays are tied. Depending on eligibility, delay length, and whether any prior refund exists, the operator may route the case to delivery support, human review, or refund review. These are review paths only: support should not promise a refund, change an order, or claim an outcome before the proper review is completed.

Delayed delivery support starts by reviewing the delivery timeline and explaining the available support path. For general policy, support may help check status, clarify expected next steps, and escalate cases that appear significantly delayed. In this sandbox policy, a full customer-specific review would use verified records, select the most delayed order, and consider eligibility and prior refunds before recommending delivery support, human review, or refund review. No refund, order change, or outcome is guaranteed from this general explanation.

Delayed delivery support generally starts by checking the order’s current status and how late it is against the applicable support policy. If an order is still in transit or only slightly delayed, the recommended path is usually delivery support, such as status guidance or next-step instructions. For longer delays, the case may be reviewed for refund eligibility, but support staff should not promise or issue a refund without the required records and review. Prior refunds can also require human review to avoid duplicate outcomes.

Delayed delivery support generally starts by checking the delivery status and how late the order is. In cases where an order is significantly delayed, the support operator may review whether further escalation is appropriate under policy. This explanation is general only and does not use or confirm any customer-specific records.

These are operator recommendations only; no refund, order change, or financial action is issued or guaranteed in this explanation.
